# Setup reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/reference-docs.py from the isocast binary; do not edit. -->

A setup is one document: sources, scenes, the canvas, recording and
streaming settings. Write it as TOML (or JSON); `isocast setup check FILE`
validates it, `isocast plan` and `isocast apply` change the live one, and
`isocast setup schema` prints the JSON Schema these tables come from.
Everything is addressed by `id`. The stream key is never part of a setup.

## Setup

A complete session description.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio` | [AudioSetup](#audiosetup) | How sources' balance pans them, and where monitored sources play. |
| `canvas` (required) | [Canvas](#canvas) | The composited output canvas. |
| `canvases` | list of [VerticalCanvas](#verticalcanvas) | More canvases, each with its own id, size, frame rate, scene (or the main one's, laid out its own way), recording and streams, for streaming one show to several platforms in their own shapes (#84): `[[canvases]]` with an `id`, otherwise as `[vertical]`. |
| `developer` | [DeveloperSettings](#developersettings) | Developer mode: verbose logs and timing traces (the profile's). |
| `governor` | [GovernorSettings](#governorsettings) | |
| `hotkeys` | [Config](#config) | Profile hotkeys. Absent/empty keeps legacy profiles unchanged. |
| `keyframes` | list of [Keyframes](#keyframes) | Keyframe sets, by id, that scene items' `animations` play (CSS's `@keyframes`). |
| `name` (required) | string | Human-readable name of this setup. |
| `recording` (required) | [Recording](#recording) | How recordings are written. |
| `scenes` | list of [Scene](#scene) | Arrangements of sources on the canvas. Default `[]`. |
| `sources` | list of [Source](#source) | Every input the session can use. Default `[]`. |
| `stream` | [StreamSettings](#streamsettings) (optional) | Live streaming of the program, if set up. The stream key is never part of a setup: `isocast stream key set` keeps it in the Keychain. |
| `transition` | [Transition](#transition) | How the program changes scenes unless a switch says otherwise. |
| `version` (required) | integer | Setup format version. Must be 1. |
| `vertical` | [VerticalCanvas](#verticalcanvas) (optional) | A second, vertical canvas (for Shorts, Reels, TikTok) showing the same scenes, with its own recording and stream. Absent: none. |
| `virtual_camera` | [VirtualCameraSettings](#virtualcamerasettings) | |

## AudioSetup

Audio settings for the whole setup.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `monitoring_device` | string | The output device monitored sources play through: "default" (the system output, following it when it changes), or an id, name or part of a name from `isocast devices`. Default `"default"`. |
| `pan_law` | [PanLaw](#panlaw) | How a source's `balance` lowers the side it moves away from. Default `"sine"`. |

## PanLaw

How balance moves a source between left and right. Each is the classic pan law of that name, taken relative to the centre and never above it: at 0 both sides are as captured, moving towards one side lowers the other until it is silent at the end, and the near side stays as it is.

One of:

- `"sine"`: Sine/cosine: the far side follows √2·sin(π/4·(1 − \|balance\|)), −5.3 dB at a balance of ±0.5.
- `"square"`: Square root (constant power): √(1 − \|balance\|), −3 dB at ±0.5.
- `"linear"`: Linear: 1 − \|balance\|, −6 dB at ±0.5.

## Canvas

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fps` (required) | integer | Frames per second, from 1 to 240. |
| `height` (required) | integer | An even number of pixels from 16 to 8192. |
| `width` (required) | integer | An even number of pixels from 16 to 8192. |

## VerticalCanvas

Another canvas, upright by default, that shows the setup's scenes: the `[vertical]` canvas or one of `[[canvases]]`. A scene is laid out on it by its arrangement for it (`vertical`, or `canvases.<id>`) if it has one, else it shows the main picture fitted inside this canvas and centred (letterboxed; items placed by `layout` are laid out again on this canvas's size). Its program has the same audio mix as the main one (`recording.program.audio`).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `follow_main` | boolean | Show the scene the main canvas has on air, switching with it. False lets the vertical canvas put its own scene on air. |
| `fps` | integer (optional) | Frames per second, from 1 to 240; the main canvas's if absent. |
| `height` | integer | An even number of pixels from 16 to 8192. Default `1920`. |
| `id` | string (optional) | Its id in `[[canvases]]` (lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 32; not `main` or `vertical`), as requests' `canvas` names it. Absent on `[vertical]`, whose id is `vertical`. |
| `name` | string (optional) | Display label, like "YouTube Shorts". Defaults to the id. |
| `recording` | [VerticalRecording](#verticalrecording) (optional) | The vertical program recording. Absent: not recorded. |
| `stream` | [StreamSettings](#streamsettings) (optional) | Live streaming of the vertical program, if set up (its own service; the key stays in the Keychain). |
| `width` | integer | An even number of pixels from 16 to 8192. Default `1080`. |

## VerticalRecording

How the vertical program is recorded, in `recording.folder` alongside the main program. Its sound is the main program's mix (`recording.program.audio`): both canvases share one audio mix.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio` | list of string | Must be empty: the vertical program has the main program's audio mix (`recording.program.audio`). |
| `enabled` | boolean |  Default `true`. |
| `encoder` | [Encoder](#encoder) |  Default `{"bit_depth": 8, "codec": "hevc", "container": "mov", "quality": "high"}`. |
| `filename` | string | File name without extension. Tokens: {date}, {time}. Must differ from `recording.program.filename`. Default `"{date} {time} vertical"`. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `width` | integer (optional) | The file's size, if not the vertical canvas's (each side even, from 16 up to the vertical canvas's). |

## Encoder

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bit_depth` | integer | 8 or 10. 10-bit HEVC uses the Main 10 profile, which avoids banding in gradients. ProRes is always 10-bit; H.264 can only be 8-bit. The incredible HEVC preset promotes 8 to 10. Default `8`. Max 255. |
| `codec` (required) | [Codec](#codec) | |
| `container` | [Container](#container) |  Default `"mov"`. |
| `quality` | [EncoderQuality](#encoderquality) | A named quality preset, or the original 1–100 constant quality. Ignored by ProRes, which is constant quality. Default `"high"`. |

## Codec

One of: `"h264"`, `"hevc"`, `"prores422_proxy"`, `"prores422_lt"`, `"prores422"`, `"prores422_hq"`, `"prores4444"`.

## Container

One of: `"mov"`, `"mp4"`.

## EncoderQuality

Numbers stay numbers and preset names stay names in setup files and API replies. See docs/recording.md for the measured preset ladder.

One of:

- [QualityPreset](#qualitypreset)
- integer

## QualityPreset

One of: `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"very_high"`, `"incredible"`.

## StreamSettings

Streaming the program (the canvas and the program mix) to a service over RTMP or RTMPS, as H.264 and AAC.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio_bitrate_kbps` | integer | AAC audio bitrate in kb/s, held constant (silence too, as services expect): 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256 or 320. Default `160`. |
| `destinations` | list of [StreamDestination](#streamdestination) | More places to stream the same program to at once, each with its own key, state and reconnects. A destination with the same encode settings as another shares its encoder; one with its own `video_bitrate_kbps` or size gets an encoder of its own if this Mac's encoders have room. |
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether `stream start` (without `only`) streams to this section's own service, the main destination (id `main`). Its encode settings stay the other destinations' defaults while it is off. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `keyframe_interval_seconds` | integer | Seconds between keyframes. Twitch and YouTube ask for 2. Default `2`. |
| `rate_control` | [RateControl](#ratecontrol) (optional) | How the encoder keeps to `video_bitrate_kbps`: `constant` (the default: the full rate every second, padding still scenes, as YouTube's and Twitch's guidelines ask) or `average` (fewer bits when the picture is still, overshooting very busy scenes a little less). |
| `reconnect` | [Reconnect](#reconnect) | Connect again after the connection drops. |
| `server` | string (optional) | The ingest server without the stream key: `rtmp://host[:port]/app` or `rtmps://host[:port]/app`. Required for `custom` and `kick` (each Kick channel has its own); for the other services it replaces their default server (for example a nearer Twitch ingest). |
| `service` (required) | [StreamService](#streamservice) | Where to stream. A service fills in its ingest server; `custom` needs `server`. |
| `video_bitrate_kbps` | integer | Video bitrate in kb/s, held near constant as services ask. Default `6000`. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | The size sent, if not the canvas's: the encoder scales the program to it. Without it, a canvas larger than 1920×1080 (1080×1920 upright) is scaled down to fit, as most services take 1080p at most. Each side is an even number from 16 to 4096. |

## StreamDestination

Another place to stream the program to (see [`StreamSettings::destinations`]). What it doesn't set comes from the `[stream]` section; reconnecting always does.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio_bitrate_kbps` | integer (optional) | Its own AAC bitrate; `[stream]`'s if absent. |
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether `stream start` (without `only`) streams here. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `id` (required) | string | Its id (lowercase letters, digits and dashes; not `main`), as `isocast stream start --only` and the key commands name it. |
| `keyframe_interval_seconds` | integer (optional) | Its own seconds between keyframes; `[stream]`'s if absent. |
| `rate_control` | [RateControl](#ratecontrol) (optional) | Its own rate control; `[stream]`'s if absent. |
| `server` | string (optional) | The ingest server without the stream key, as for `[stream]`. |
| `service` (required) | [StreamService](#streamservice) | |
| `video_bitrate_kbps` | integer (optional) | Its own video bitrate; `[stream]`'s if absent. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Its own size sent; `[stream]`'s if absent. Give both or neither. |

## RateControl

How a stream's encoder keeps to its bitrate.

One of:

- `"average"`: About the bitrate on average: fewer bits for still pictures.
- `"constant"`: The bitrate every second, still pictures padded.

## StreamService

A streaming service. Presets use the service's documented RTMPS ingest (see `docs/streaming.md`).

One of:

- `"twitch"` \| `"youtube"` \| `"facebook"`
- `"custom"`: Any RTMP or RTMPS server, given as `server`.
- `"kick"`: Kick: give your channel's Stream URL (Creator Dashboard → Channel → Stream URL and Key) as `server`.

## Reconnect

Reconnecting after the connection to the server drops.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `delay_seconds` | integer | Seconds to wait before each attempt. Default `2`. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  Default `true`. |
| `max_retries` | integer | Attempts before giving up (the stream then shows `failed`). Default `25`. |

## DeveloperSettings

The profile's developer mode.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_off_hours` | integer | Turn it off by itself this many hours after it was turned on; 0 keeps it on until turned off. Default `24`. |
| `enabled` | boolean | Log every API call and debug messages from capture, the compositor, encoders, writers, streaming and updates, and trace frame timing each second while recording, into their own log segments (200 MiB budget, separate from the ordinary logs). Default `false`. |

## GovernorSettings

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `allow_iso_thinning` | boolean | The user's explicit choice to let the governor skip ISO pictures under pressure (off by default). Skipped pictures are lost from the file for good. Off, every ISO counts as pinned; the native encoder safety controller still sheds ISO frames on real overload. Default `false`. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  Default `true`. |
| `pins` | list of string | Settings the governor must not override. Native overload protection still applies; a pin cannot guarantee that hardware delivers frames. Default `[]`. |

## Config

Lossless, non-critical configuration on a setup/profile. Unknown or invalid entries survive interchange but never execute. Only hotkeys_set uses the strict Binding type directly. None distinguishes omission from explicit {}.

## Keyframes

A keyframe set: how an item's properties change over one run of an animation, as stops along it (CSS's `@keyframes`).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `frames` (required) | list of [Keyframe](#keyframe) | The stops, in order of `at`. A property no stop at 0 (or 1) sets runs from (or to) the item's own value, as in CSS. |
| `id` (required) | string | What animations call it. |

## Keyframe

One stop of a keyframe set: the values it gives at `at`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `at` (required) | number | How far through a run it is, from 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). |
| `background` | [Color](#color) (optional) | In place of the item's background colour. |
| `border_color` | [Color](#color) (optional) | In place of its border's colour. |
| `border_width` | number (optional) | In place of its border's width, in pixels. |
| `crop` | [Crop](#crop) (optional) | In place of its crop, in pixels of its picture. |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) (optional) | How the stretch from this stop to the next speeds up and slows down, in place of the animation's `easing`. |
| `opacity` | number (optional) | Multiplies the item's opacity (and its children's): 0 to 1. |
| `radius` | [Radius](#radius) (optional) | In place of its corner radius. |
| `rotate` | number (optional) | Turns the item about its centre, in degrees clockwise. |
| `scale` | number (optional) | Scales the item about its centre (1 is its size; 0 or more). |
| `shadow` | [Shadow](#shadow) (optional) | In place of its shadow. |
| `translate` | list of [Length](#length) (optional) | Moves the item [x, y]: pixels, or `"50%"` of its own width and height. Applied around its own `style.transform`, like CSS's `translate` property. |

## Color

A colour as `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`.

Type: string.

## Crop

Pixels cut from the edges of a source.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bottom` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `left` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `right` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `top` | integer |  Default `0`. |

## Easing

How motion speeds up and slows down: one of four names, or CSS's `cubic-bezier()` and `steps()`.

One of:

- [EasingName](#easingname)
- [CubicBezierForm](#cubicbezierform)
- [StepsForm](#stepsform)

## EasingName

How motion speeds up and slows down over a transition.

One of:

- `"linear"`: At an even speed.
- `"ease_in"`: Starting slowly.
- `"ease_out"`: Ending slowly.
- `"ease_in_out"`: Starting and ending slowly (cubic).

## CubicBezierForm

CSS's `cubic-bezier()`: `{ cubic_bezier = [x1, y1, x2, y2] }`, the two control points of a curve from (0, 0) to (1, 1), time across (x1 and x2 from 0 to 1) and progress up (y1 and y2 may overshoot).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cubic_bezier` (required) | list of number | |

## StepsForm

CSS's `steps()`: `{ steps = 4 }` or `{ steps = 4, position = "start" }`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `position` | [StepPosition](#stepposition) | Where each step jumps: `start`, `end` (the default), `both` or `none`. |
| `steps` (required) | integer | How many steps (at least 1; 2 with `position = "none"`). |

## StepPosition

Where `steps` jumps (CSS's `jump-start`, `jump-end`, `jump-both` and `jump-none`).

One of:

- `"start"`: At the start of each step: the first jump is at once.
- `"end"`: At the end of each step: the last jump is at the end.
- `"both"`: At both ends: n + 1 levels, from 0 to 1, each held as long.
- `"none"`: At neither: n levels from 0 to 1, the first and last held as long as the others.

## Radius

Corner radii in pixels.

One of:

- number
- list of number: Top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left.

## Shadow

A drop shadow under the item, following its corners.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `blur` | number | How far it blurs, in pixels. Default `0.0`. |
| `color` (required) | [Color](#color) | |
| `x` | number | Offset in pixels. Default `0.0`. |
| `y` | number |  Default `0.0`. |

## Length

A length: a number of pixels (`12`, or `"12px"`), a percentage of the parent's content box (`"50%"`, CSS's rules), or `"auto"`.

One of:

- number
- string

## Recording

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` (required) | string | Folder recordings are written to. `~` expands to the home folder. |
| `iso` | [IsoRecording](#isorecording) | Separate recordings of individual sources. Default `{"enabled": false, "encoder": {"codec": "hevc", "container": "mov", "quality": "high"}, "filename": "{SOURCE}-{date} {time}", "sources": []}`. |
| `keep_free_gb` | number | Free space, in GB, a recording never uses: it won't start without room for its estimated size plus this, and it stops cleanly, finishing every file, when free space falls below it (or below about 10 s of its files, at least 64 MB, if that is more). Default `1.0`. |
| `open_editor` | boolean | Retired with the editor (2026-10-22): read and ignored, so setups that set it still load; never written. |
| `program` (required) | [ProgramRecording](#programrecording) | The composited program recording. |
| `replay` | [ReplaySettings](#replaysettings) | The replay buffer: how much of the program it keeps. |

## IsoRecording

ISO ("isolated") recording: each listed source is written to its own file at its native resolution, on the same clock as the program recording.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio` | list of string (optional) | Audio sources written into every ISO file without a list of its own in `source_audio`. Omitted: each ISO uses its own source's sound. An explicit list (including []) preserves the chosen shared routing. A source's audio.iso can override its own sound. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  Default `false`. |
| `encoder` | [IsoEncoder](#isoencoder) |  Default `{"codec": "hevc", "container": "mov", "quality": "high"}`. |
| `filename` | string | File name without extension. Tokens: {SOURCE} (upper-case id), {source}, {date}, {time}. Default `"{SOURCE}-{date} {time}"`. |
| `filtered` | boolean | Record sources with filters as filtered (as the program shows them) rather than as captured, and audio with its audio filters (all but sidechain ducking). Keyed-out areas come out black, since the files have no transparency. |
| `source_audio` | map of list of string | Audio sources for one ISO file, by its video source's id, instead of `audio`: `{ camera = ["mic"], screen = ["desktop"] }`. An empty list records that file without audio. Sources not listed follow `audio`; a source's audio.iso still adds or drops its own sound. |
| `sources` | list of string | Video sources to record separately. Default `[]`. |

## IsoEncoder

The ISO files' encoder: [`Encoder`]'s fields, but `bit_depth` can be left out (it then stays out when saved).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bit_depth` | integer (optional) | 8 or 10, for every ISO file without a depth of its own (a source's `encoder.bit_depth`). 10-bit HEVC uses the Main 10 profile, which avoids banding in gradients, and captures displays, windows and applications in 10 bits, at more encoder work and bigger files. ProRes is always 10-bit; H.264 can only be 8-bit. A set 8 stays 8 even at the incredible preset. Left out: 8, but 10 at incredible HEVC. Max 255. |
| `codec` (required) | [Codec](#codec) | |
| `container` | [Container](#container) |  Default `"mov"`. |
| `quality` | [EncoderQuality](#encoderquality) | A named quality preset, or the original 1–100 constant quality. Ignored by ProRes, which is constant quality. Default `"high"`. |

## ProgramRecording

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio` | list of string | Audio sources mixed into the program recording. Default `[]`. |
| `enabled` | boolean |  Default `true`. |
| `encoder` (required) | [Encoder](#encoder) | |
| `filename` | string | File name without extension. Tokens: {date}, {time}. Default `"{date} {time}"`. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `width` | integer (optional) | The program file's size, if not the canvas's: the encoder scales the canvas down to it (a different shape is letterboxed), like OBS's Output (Scaled) Resolution. ISO files keep their sources' sizes. Each side is an even number from 16 up to the canvas's. |

## ReplaySettings

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `max_memory_mb` | integer | The most memory the buffer may use, in MB, from 16 to 8192. If `seconds` of the program need more (a high bitrate), the oldest seconds go and `replay_status` says the buffer is short. Default `1024`. |
| `seconds` | integer | How many seconds of the program a save covers, from 5 to 300 (the saved file starts at the keyframe before them, so it can be up to a keyframe interval longer). Default `30`. |
| `video_bitrate_kbps` | integer (optional) | The video bitrate, in kb/s, when the buffer encodes the program itself. Without it, about 0.1 bit per pixel (12 Mb/s at 1080p60), at most 40 Mb/s. While the setup has a `[stream]`, the buffer encodes as the stream does (its size, bitrate and keyframes), so a stream and the buffer share one encoder; this is then unused. |

## Scene

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `canvases` | map of [SceneLayout](#scenelayout) | Its arrangements on the setup's `[[canvases]]`, by canvas id, as `vertical` is on the vertical canvas. |
| `id` (required) | string | |
| `items` | list of [SceneItem](#sceneitem) | Items drawn back to front. Default `[]`. |
| `layout` | [Layout](#layout) (optional) | How its items with a `layout` are laid out: the scene is their root container, the size of the canvas (CSS block layout if absent). Only the fields for children apply. |
| `name` | string (optional) | |
| `transition` | [Transition](#transition) (optional) | How the program changes to this scene, in place of the setup's transition, unless a switch names its own (OBS's transition override). |
| `vertical` | [SceneLayout](#scenelayout) (optional) | Its arrangement on the setup's vertical canvas, in place of `layout` and `items`. Absent: the main picture fitted inside the vertical canvas and centred (letterboxed): items placed by `rect` are scaled and centred with it, items placed by `layout` are laid out again on the vertical canvas's size. |

## SceneLayout

How a scene is arranged on the vertical canvas, in place of its own `layout` and `items`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of [SceneItem](#sceneitem) | Items drawn back to front, in vertical canvas pixels. Default `[]`. |
| `layout` | [Layout](#layout) (optional) | How its items with a `layout` are laid out, as the scene's `layout`. |

## SceneItem

Something drawn in a scene: a video source, a scene, content (text or an image made from settings), or (with none of them) a box that is just its style, and a group for the items in `children`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `align` | [Align](#align) | Where the picture sits in the rect when it doesn't fill it, and which part shows when it overflows (OBS's alignment in the bounding box). Centred by default. |
| `animations` | list of [Animation](#animation) | Keyframe sets it plays (CSS's `animation`), each on its clock: `[{ keyframes = "slide-in", duration_ms = 400 }]`. A later one wins over an earlier one on the same property. |
| `blend` | [Blend](#blend) | How the item combines with what is drawn below it (OBS's blending modes): `normal` (the default), `additive`, `subtract`, `screen`, `multiply`, `lighten` or `darken`. Its children use their own. |
| `children` | list of [SceneItem](#sceneitem) | Items drawn on top of this one, back to front, placed relative to its rect and moved, scaled, rotated and faded with it. |
| `content` | [Content](#content) (optional) | Or text or an image the engine makes from these settings, without a source: `{ kind = "text", text = "Hi", size = 48 }` (the text source's settings; `data = "key"` shows a data key's value) or `{ kind = "image", path = "logo.png" }`. Give it an `id` to patch it. |
| `crop` | [Crop](#crop) | Pixels cut from each edge of the source before it is scaled. |
| `fit` | [Fit](#fit) | How the picture fills the rect. New API items use `none` (native size times transform scale). Omission in old files retains legacy stretch; explicitly chosen `stretch` is always saved. |
| `hide_transition` | [ItemTransition](#itemtransition) (optional) | How it disappears when hidden (OBS's hide transition). |
| `id` | string (optional) | Identifies the item for patches and transitions; its source's id if absent. Unique within its scene. |
| `layout` | [Layout](#layout) (optional) | Or where layout places it in its parent (a scene, or an item whose `layout` arranges its children), and how its own children are laid out: CSS's flexbox, grid, block and absolute positioning. Its size can come from what it shows: a source's picture size, or the canvas for a scene. |
| `locked` | boolean | Locked in the app's canvas editor (OBS's lock): it can be selected there but not moved or resized. Patches change it as usual; the engine ignores it. |
| `rect` | [Rect](#rect) (optional) | Where it is drawn, in canvas pixels (relative to its parent's rect for children); a source is scaled to fill it. Give this or `layout`: a rect is the same as `layout = { position = "absolute", left = x, top = y, width, height }`. |
| `scale_filter` | [ScaleFilter](#scalefilter) | How the picture is resampled to the size it is drawn at: `point`, `bilinear` (the default), `bicubic`, `lanczos` or `area` (OBS's scale filtering). |
| `scene` | string (optional) | Or the id of a scene it shows (OBS's nested scenes): the scene drawn at the canvas size, transparent where it shows nothing, and scaled to fill the rect like a source. |
| `show_transition` | [ItemTransition](#itemtransition) (optional) | How it appears when it becomes visible (OBS's show transition): a `fade`, or a `slide` in from a side; at once if absent. |
| `source` | string (optional) | The id of the video source it shows; absent for a box or group. |
| `style` | [Style](#style) | |
| `visible` | boolean |  Default `true`. |

## Align

Where a picture sits in its item's rect.

One of: `"center"`, `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"`, `"top_left"`, `"top_right"`, `"bottom_left"`, `"bottom_right"`.

## Animation

A keyframe set played on an item (CSS's `animation`).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `delay_ms` | integer | How long after its clock starts it starts, in milliseconds; less than 0 starts it part of the way through. |
| `direction` | [PlayDirection](#playdirection) | Which way runs go: `normal` (the default), `reverse`, `alternate` (forwards, then backwards) or `alternate_reverse`. |
| `duration_ms` (required) | integer | How long one run takes, in milliseconds. |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) | How each stretch between stops speeds up and slows down, unless a stop says otherwise (as CSS's `animation-timing-function`): `ease_in_out` if absent. |
| `fill` | [Fill](#fill) | Whether its first stop holds before it starts and its last after it ends: `both` (the default), `forwards`, `backwards` or `none`. |
| `iterations` | [Iterations](#iterations) | How many runs: a number (1 if absent; 2.5 ends half way through the third) or `"infinite"`. |
| `keyframes` (required) | string | The id of the keyframe set it plays. |
| `start` | [AnimationStart](#animationstart) | The clock it runs on: `on_air` (the default; from when the program, or studio mode's preview, starts showing the item's scene, again each time), `shown` (from when the item appears or is made visible) or `clock` (the engine's clock: loops stay in step across scene switches and recordings). |

## PlayDirection

Which way an animation's runs go (CSS's `animation-direction`).

One of:

- `"normal"`: From the first stop to the last, every run.
- `"reverse"`: From the last stop to the first, every run (easings run backwards too).
- `"alternate"`: Forwards, then backwards, and so on.
- `"alternate_reverse"`: Backwards, then forwards, and so on.

## Fill

Whether an animation's values hold outside its runs (CSS's `animation-fill-mode`).

One of:

- `"both"`: Its start holds before it starts, and its end after it ends.
- `"forwards"`: Its end holds after it ends; before it starts the item looks as its own values say.
- `"backwards"`: Its start holds before it starts; after it ends the item looks as its own values say.
- `"none"`: Neither: outside its runs the item looks as its own values say.

## Iterations

How many times an animation runs.

One of:

- number
- [Infinite](#infinite)

## Infinite

One of:

- `"infinite"`: For as long as its clock runs.

## AnimationStart

The clock an animation runs on.

One of:

- `"on_air"`: From when the program (or studio mode's preview, which keeps its own) starts showing the item's scene, again each time it does; a scene shown inside another starts with that one.
- `"shown"`: From when the item appears (with the engine, or added by a change) or is made visible.
- `"clock"`: The engine's clock, from when it started: never restarts, so loops stay in step across scene switches and recordings.

## Blend

How an item's colours combine with what is already drawn below it, channel by channel, in encoded (not linear) values like OBS's "sRGB off" blending method. The item's opacity fades the effect.

One of:

- `"normal"`: Drawn over what is below, by its alpha.
- `"additive"`: Added to what is below: lights, glows, flares on black.
- `"subtract"`: Taken away from what is below.
- `"screen"`: Brightens: one minus the product of the inverses, so black leaves what is below as it was.
- `"multiply"`: Darkens: the product, so white leaves what is below as it was.
- `"lighten"`: The lighter of the two.
- `"darken"`: The darker of the two.

## Content

What an item shows in place of a source or scene: text, or an image, made by the engine from these settings (the text and image sources' own, `kind` saying which). It isn't a source: it has no ISO file and opens nothing; it is drawn again only when its settings, or the data key it shows, change, and items showing the same content share one picture. Text placed by `layout` wraps at the width its box gets.

One of:

- `kind = "text"`: [TextSource](#textsource) Text, as a text source draws it: from `text`, a `file` or a `data` key.
- `kind = "image"`: [ImageSource](#imagesource) An image file, as an image source shows it (an animated GIF shows its first frame; use an image source to play it).

## TextSource

Text (OBS's Text source), from `text`, a file or a data key, in a font, with an optional outline, shadow and background.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `align` | [TextAlign](#textalign) |  Default `"left"`. |
| `background` | [Color](#color) (optional) | A colour behind the text box. |
| `color` | [Color](#color) |  Default `"#ffffff"`. |
| `data` | string (optional) | Or a data key whose value it shows, drawn again when the value changes (`isocast data set KEY VALUE`, MCP set_data): strings as they are, numbers formatted, anything else as JSON; nothing while the key isn't set. |
| `file` | string (optional) | Or a file to read the text from, re-read when it changes: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. |
| `font` | string | A font family installed on this Mac, like "Helvetica Neue" or "Menlo". Default `"Helvetica Neue"`. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `italic` | boolean |  Default `false`. |
| `line_height` | number | Line spacing, as a multiple of the font size. Default `1.2000000476837158`. |
| `outline` | [TextOutline](#textoutline) (optional) | |
| `padding` | integer | Space around the text, in pixels. Default `0`. |
| `shadow` | [TextShadow](#textshadow) (optional) | |
| `size` | number | Font size in pixels. Default `72.0`. |
| `text` | string (optional) | |
| `weight` | integer | 100 (thin) to 900 (black); 400 is regular, 700 bold. Default `400`. Max 65535. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | A fixed size in pixels; the text's own size if absent. Set it for text that changes, so the source keeps one size. `align` places the lines across this width, inside the padding. |
| `wrap_width` | integer (optional) | Wrap lines at this width in pixels; otherwise each line of the text is one line. |

## TextAlign

One of: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`.

## TextOutline

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` (required) | [Color](#color) | |
| `width` (required) | number | Width in pixels. |

## TextShadow

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` (required) | [Color](#color) | |
| `x` | number | Offset in pixels. Default `2.0`. |
| `y` | number |  Default `2.0`. |

## ImageSource

An image file: PNG, JPEG, GIF (animated ones play), WebP, BMP, TGA or SVG.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `path` (required) | string | The file: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | For SVG, the size to draw it at; its own size if absent. |

## Fit

How an item's picture (what is left after its crop) fills the item's rect, like CSS `object-fit`; OBS calls these bounding box types. The rect clips the picture, and its background shows where the picture doesn't reach.

One of:

- `"stretch"`: Stretched to the rect, whatever its shape (OBS: stretch to bounds).
- `"contain"`: As large as fits inside the rect, keeping its shape (OBS: scale to inner bounds).
- `"cover"`: Covering the rect, keeping its shape; what overflows is cut off (OBS: scale to outer bounds, cropped to the bounding box).
- `"width"`: As wide as the rect, keeping its shape (OBS: scale to width of bounds).
- `"height"`: As tall as the rect, keeping its shape (OBS: scale to height of bounds).
- `"scale_down"`: Like `contain`, but never larger than its own size (OBS: maximum size only).
- `"none"`: At its own size in pixels, before the item's transform (OBS: no bounds).

## ItemTransition

How a scene item appears when it becomes visible, or disappears when hidden (OBS's show and hide transitions).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | Where a slide comes in from (or goes out to): `left` (the default), `right`, `up` or `down`. |
| `duration_ms` | integer | How long it takes, in milliseconds (300 if absent, at most 10 s). Default `300`. |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) | |
| `kind` (required) | [ItemTransitionKind](#itemtransitionkind) | |

## Direction

Which way something moves across the canvas.

One of: `"left"`, `"right"`, `"up"`, `"down"`.

## ItemTransitionKind

One of:

- `"fade"`: Fades in or out.
- `"slide"`: The picture slides in from (or out to) a side of the item, within the item's rect.

## Layout

Where an item goes in its parent, and how its children are laid out: CSS's properties of the same names in snake case. All are optional. A scene's layout takes only the fields for children.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `align_content` | [JustifyContent](#justifycontent) (optional) | |
| `align_items` | [AlignItems](#alignitems) (optional) | |
| `align_self` | [AlignItems](#alignitems) (optional) | Its own `align_items` in a flex or grid parent. |
| `aspect_ratio` | number (optional) | Width divided by height, used where only one of them is known. |
| `bottom` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `direction` | [FlexDirection](#flexdirection) (optional) | A flex container's main axis: `row` (the default), `column`, `row_reverse` or `column_reverse`. |
| `display` | [LayoutDisplay](#layoutdisplay) (optional) | How its children are laid out: `block` (stacked top to bottom, the default), `flex` or `grid`. |
| `flex_basis` | [Length](#length) (optional) | Its size along a flex row or column before growing or shrinking: `auto` (the default) is its width or height, else what it shows (a picture's own size). `flex_basis = 0` with `flex_grow` shares the room by `flex_grow` alone (CSS's `flex: 1`). |
| `flex_grow` | number (optional) | How much of the free room in a flex row or column it takes, against its siblings' (0, the default, takes none). |
| `flex_shrink` | number (optional) | How much it gives up when a flex row or column is too full (1 by default). |
| `gap` | [Gap](#gap) (optional) | Room between a flex or grid container's children: one length, or [row gap, column gap]. |
| `grid_auto_flow` | [GridAutoFlow](#gridautoflow) (optional) | How a grid places children without `grid_row`/`grid_column`: `row` (the default), `column`, `row_dense` or `column_dense`. |
| `grid_column` | [GridLine](#gridline) (optional) | The grid columns it spans, as `grid_row`. |
| `grid_row` | [GridLine](#gridline) (optional) | The grid rows it spans: a line (`2`), `"1 / 3"`, `"span 2"` or `"2 / span 3"`. |
| `grid_template_columns` | [GridTracks](#gridtracks) (optional) | A grid's columns, as in CSS: `"1fr 2fr 200px"`, `"repeat(3, 1fr)"`, `"minmax(200px, 1fr) auto"`. |
| `grid_template_rows` | [GridTracks](#gridtracks) (optional) | A grid's rows, as `grid_template_columns`. |
| `height` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `inset` | [Sides](#sides) (optional) | `top`, `right`, `bottom` and `left` at once (each one given wins). |
| `justify_content` | [JustifyContent](#justifycontent) (optional) | |
| `justify_self` | [AlignItems](#alignitems) (optional) | Where it sits across its grid cell. |
| `left` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `margin` | [Sides](#sides) (optional) | |
| `max_height` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `max_width` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `min_height` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `min_width` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `overflow` | [Overflow](#overflow) (optional) | `hidden` clips its children (shadows too) to its rounded rect; `visible`, the default, doesn't. |
| `padding` | [Sides](#sides) (optional) | |
| `position` | [Position](#position) (optional) | `relative` (in its parent's flow, the default) or `absolute` (placed by `left`, `top`, `right` and `bottom` within its parent, taking no room from its siblings). |
| `right` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `top` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `width` | [Length](#length) (optional) | |
| `wrap` | [FlexWrap](#flexwrap) (optional) | Whether a flex container's children wrap onto more lines: `nowrap` (the default), `wrap` or `wrap_reverse`. |

## JustifyContent

How children share the room along an axis (CSS `justify-content` and `align-content`).

One of: `"start"`, `"end"`, `"flex_start"`, `"flex_end"`, `"center"`, `"stretch"`, `"space_between"`, `"space_around"`, `"space_evenly"`.

## AlignItems

Where children sit across an axis (CSS `align-items`, `align-self`, `justify-self`).

One of: `"start"`, `"end"`, `"flex_start"`, `"flex_end"`, `"center"`, `"baseline"`, `"stretch"`.

## FlexDirection

One of: `"row"`, `"column"`, `"row_reverse"`, `"column_reverse"`.

## LayoutDisplay

One of: `"block"`, `"flex"`, `"grid"`.

## Gap

The room between children: one length for both, or [row gap, column gap].

One of:

- [Length](#length)
- list of [Length](#length)

## GridAutoFlow

One of: `"row"`, `"column"`, `"row_dense"`, `"column_dense"`.

## GridLine

Where a grid item starts and ends along one axis: a line number, or a string as CSS writes `grid-row`.

One of:

- integer
- string

## GridTracks

A grid track list in CSS's syntax: sizes (`200px`, `25%`, `1fr`, `auto`, `min-content`, `max-content`, `minmax(MIN, MAX)`) and `repeat(N, ...)` (or `repeat(auto-fill, ...)`, `repeat(auto-fit, ...)`), separated by spaces.

Type: string.

## Sides

Lengths for the four sides, as CSS's `margin`, `padding` and `inset` take them.

One of:

- [Length](#length)
- list of [Length](#length): Vertical, horizontal.
- list of [Length](#length): Top, right, bottom, left.

## Overflow

One of: `"visible"`, `"hidden"`.

## Position

One of: `"relative"`, `"absolute"`.

## FlexWrap

One of: `"nowrap"`, `"wrap"`, `"wrap_reverse"`.

## Rect

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` (required) | integer | |
| `width` (required) | integer | |
| `x` (required) | integer | |
| `y` (required) | integer | |

## ScaleFilter

How a picture is resampled to a new size.

One of:

- `"bilinear"`
- `"point"`: Nearest pixel: blocky, for pixel art.
- `"bicubic"`: Sharper than bilinear.
- `"lanczos"`: Sharpest, with slight ringing.
- `"area"`: Averages the pixels each one covers: best for shrinking a lot.

## Style

How an item looks, in CSS terms.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | [Color](#color) (optional) | A colour behind the item, which a box is filled with: `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`. |
| `border` | [Border](#border) (optional) | |
| `opacity` | number | 0 (invisible) to 1 (opaque), applied to children too. |
| `radius` | [Radius](#radius) | Corner radius in pixels: one for all corners, or [top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left]. |
| `shadow` | [Shadow](#shadow) (optional) | |
| `transform` | [Transform](#transform) | |

## Border

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` (required) | [Color](#color) | |
| `width` (required) | number | Width in pixels, drawn inside the rect. |

## Transform

Moves, scales, rotates and flips an item around its centre.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `flip_horizontal` | boolean | Mirrored left to right, before it is rotated: its picture, children, border and shadow. |
| `flip_vertical` | boolean | Mirrored top to bottom, before it is rotated. |
| `rotate` | number | Degrees, clockwise. Default `0.0`. |
| `scale` | number |  Default `1.0`. |
| `translate` | list of number | [x, y] in pixels. Default `[0.0, 0.0]`. |

## Transition

How the program changes from one scene to the next.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `duration_ms` | integer | How long it takes, in milliseconds (300 if absent, at most 10 s). A cut ignores it, and a stinger lasts as long as its video. Default `300`. |

Plus one of these, chosen by its tag:

- `kind = "cut"`. Straight to the next scene.
- `kind = "fade"`. The next scene fades in over the current one.
- `kind = "swipe"`: [Swipe](#swipe) The next scene slides in over the current one, or the current one slides away to uncover it.
- `kind = "slide"`: [Slide](#slide) The next scene pushes the current one off the canvas.
- `kind = "fade_to_color"`: [FadeToColor](#fadetocolor) The current scene fades to a colour, then the colour fades to the next scene.
- `kind = "luma_wipe"`: [LumaWipe](#lumawipe) The next scene appears in the order of a greyscale pattern's brightness, dark first.
- `kind = "stinger"`: [Stinger](#stinger) A video plays over the switch, hiding it (OBS's Stinger).
- `kind = "move"`: [Move](#move) Items in both scenes (the same id, showing the same thing) move, resize, turn and fade to their new place; the others fade out or in.

## Swipe

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | Which way the moving scene goes: left (it comes in from the right edge, or leaves by the left), right, up or down. Default `"left"`. |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) |  Default `"ease_in_out"`. |
| `swipe_in` | boolean | The next scene slides in over the current one (true, the default), or the current one slides away to uncover the next (false). Default `true`. |

## Slide

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [Direction](#direction) | Which way both scenes move: left (the next comes in from the right edge), right, up or down. Default `"left"`. |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) |  Default `"ease_in_out"`. |

## FadeToColor

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | [Color](#color) | The colour passed through (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`; black by default). Default `"#000000"`. |
| `switch_point` | number | How far through the transition, 0 to 100 (%), the colour is at its fullest and the scenes switch behind it. Default `50.0`. |

## LumaWipe

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `image` | string (optional) | Or a picture whose brightness gives the order (dark first), stretched over the canvas: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. If it can't be read, the pattern is used. |
| `invert` | boolean | Reverse the order: bright first. Default `false`. |
| `pattern` | [LumaPattern](#lumapattern) |  Default `"horizontal"`. |
| `softness` | number | How soft the edge is, 0 (sharp) to 1. Default `0.029999999329447746`. |

## LumaPattern

A built-in greyscale pattern for a luma wipe; the next scene appears where it is darkest first.

One of:

- `"horizontal"`: From the left edge to the right.
- `"vertical"`: From the top edge to the bottom.
- `"diagonal"`: From the top left corner to the bottom right.
- `"barn_door_horizontal"`: From a vertical line down the middle out to the left and right.
- `"barn_door_vertical"`: From a horizontal line across the middle out to the top and bottom.
- `"box"`: A rectangle growing from the centre.
- `"circle"`: A circle growing from the centre.
- `"diamond"`: A diamond growing from the centre.
- `"clock"`: A hand sweeping clockwise from twelve o'clock.
- `"blinds_horizontal"`: Eight horizontal bands, each wiping down.
- `"blinds_vertical"`: Eight vertical bands, each wiping right.
- `"checkerboard"`: A checkerboard of squares wiping right, the white squares after the black.

## Stinger

A video played over the switch (OBS's Stinger). It lasts as long as the video. Transparent parts need a video with alpha (ProRes 4444 or HEVC with alpha in a .mov, or VP9 or VP8 with alpha in a .webm, as OBS uses), or a matte.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cut_point_ms` | integer (optional) | When the scenes switch behind the video, in milliseconds from its start; half way through if absent. Not used with a matte. |
| `file` (required) | string | The video: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. It must be in the setup's transitions when a recording starts, which loads it. |
| `matte` | [Matte](#matte) (optional) | A track matte in the same video (OBS's track matte): where it is white the next scene shows, where black the current one, and grey blends them; the video's other half plays on top. |

## Matte

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `invert` | boolean | Swap black and white. Default `false`. |
| `layout` | [MatteLayout](#mattelayout) |  Default `"side_by_side"`. |

## MatteLayout

Where the matte is in the stinger's video.

One of:

- `"side_by_side"`: The picture on the left half, the matte on the right.
- `"stacked"`: The picture on the top half, the matte below.

## Move

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) |  Default `"ease_in_out"`. |

## Source

One input. `id` is the stable machine identifier; `name` is a label.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audio` | [AudioSettings](#audiosettings) | For audio sources: the program mix and sync settings. |
| `audio_filters` | list of [AudioFilter](#audiofilter) | For audio sources: filters run on the sound, in order, before the program mix (ISO files keep it as captured unless `recording.iso.filtered`). |
| `encoder` | [SourceEncoder](#sourceencoder) | For video sources: how its own ISO file is encoded, over `recording.iso.encoder`. Left out, it follows the recording settings. |
| `filters` | list of [Filter](#filter) | For video sources: effect filters run on the picture, in order, wherever it is shown (ISO files keep it as captured). |
| `id` (required) | string | Stable identifier, lowercase letters, digits and dashes. |
| `name` | string (optional) | Display label. Defaults to the id. |

Plus one of these, chosen by its tag:

- `kind = "display"`: [DisplaySource](#displaysource)
- `kind = "window"`: [WindowSource](#windowsource)
- `kind = "application"`: [ApplicationSource](#applicationsource)
- `kind = "application_audio"`: [ApplicationAudioSource](#applicationaudiosource)
- `kind = "camera"`: [CameraSource](#camerasource)
- `kind = "microphone"`: [MicrophoneSource](#microphonesource)
- `kind = "system_audio"`: [SystemAudioSource](#systemaudiosource)
- `kind = "color"`: [ColorSource](#colorsource)
- `kind = "image"`: [ImageSource](#imagesource)
- `kind = "slideshow"`: [SlideshowSource](#slideshowsource)
- `kind = "text"`: [TextSource](#textsource)
- `kind = "media"`: [MediaSource](#mediasource)
- `kind = "browser"`: [BrowserSource](#browsersource)
- `kind = "test_pattern"`: [TestPatternSource](#testpatternsource)
- `kind = "tone"`: [ToneSource](#tonesource)

## AudioSettings

How an audio source sounds in the program mix, and its sync offset. ISO files keep the source's audio as captured, only shifted by the offset.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `balance` | number | Where it sits between left (−1) and right (1) in the program mix; 0, the centre, keeps both sides as captured. `audio.pan_law` says how the far side is lowered. Mono sources start centred. Default `0.0`. |
| `gain_db` | number | Volume change in the program mix, in dB (0 keeps it as captured). Default `0.0`. |
| `iso` | boolean (optional) | Include this source's own sound in its ISO. Absent follows the ISO audio policy; false is an explicit opt-out, true an explicit opt-in. |
| `monitor` | [Monitoring](#monitoring) | Whether it is heard through the monitoring device (`audio.monitoring_device`) while recording, after gain, mute and balance. Default `"off"`. |
| `mono` | boolean | Downmix stereo to mono in the program and monitoring, before balance: (left + right) / 2 in both channels. Raw ISO audio stays as captured. |
| `muted` | boolean | Left out of the program mix. Default `false`. |
| `offset_ms` | integer | Shift the audio later (positive) or earlier, in milliseconds, in every file, to line it up with the video. Default `0`. |

## Monitoring

Whether a source is heard through the monitoring device, as in OBS's Advanced Audio Properties.

One of:

- `"off"`: Not heard (Monitor Off).
- `"monitor_only"`: Heard, but left out of the program mix; ISO files still have it (Monitor Only).
- `"monitor_and_output"`: Heard, and in the program mix (Monitor and Output).

## AudioFilter

One filter in a source's audio chain.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | A filter that is off is skipped. |
| `id` | string (optional) | Identifies the filter for patches; its kind if absent. Unique within its source. |

Plus one of these, chosen by its tag:

- `kind = "gain"`: [Gain](#gain)
- `kind = "invert_polarity"`: [InvertPolarity](#invertpolarity)
- `kind = "noise_gate"`: [NoiseGate](#noisegate)
- `kind = "noise_suppression"`: [NoiseSuppression](#noisesuppression)
- `kind = "compressor"`: [Compressor](#compressor)
- `kind = "limiter"`: [Limiter](#limiter)
- `kind = "expander"`: [Expander](#expander)
- `kind = "upward_compressor"`: [UpwardCompressor](#upwardcompressor)
- `kind = "equalizer"`: [Equalizer](#equalizer)

## Gain

Raises or lowers the volume (OBS's Gain).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `gain_db` | number | −30 to 30 dB. Default `0.0`. |

## InvertPolarity

Flips the waveform upside down, to fix a microphone that cancels another out (OBS's Invert Polarity).

Type: object.

## NoiseGate

Silences the sound while it is quieter than a threshold, cutting background noise between words (OBS's Noise Gate).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `attack_ms` | number | 1 to 10000 ms to fade in when opening. Default `25.0`. |
| `close_threshold_db` | number | −96 to 0 dBFS: an open gate closes when the sound falls below this. Set it above the background noise. Default `-32.0`. |
| `hold_ms` | number | 0 to 10000 ms to stay open after the sound falls below the close threshold, so pauses between words don't close it. Default `200.0`. |
| `open_threshold_db` | number | −96 to 0 dBFS: a closed gate opens when the sound rises above this. Set it a little below your voice. Default `-26.0`. |
| `release_ms` | number | 1 to 10000 ms to fade out when closing. Default `150.0`. |

## NoiseSuppression

Removes background noise (fans, hum, hiss) while keeping voices, with RNNoise, a small neural network (OBS's Noise Suppression, RNNoise method). It works 20 ms behind, which the program mix and filtered ISO files make up for, so the sound stays in sync.

Type: object.

## Compressor

Turns down the sound above a threshold, evening out loud and quiet parts; or, with a sidechain source, turns this source down while that one makes sound (ducking music under a voice) (OBS's Compressor).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `attack_ms` | number | 1 to 500 ms to react when the sound gets louder. Default `6.0`. |
| `output_gain_db` | number | −32 to 32 dB added afterwards to bring the level back up; not applied when ducking with a sidechain source. Default `0.0`. |
| `ratio` | number | 1 to 32: how much sound above the threshold is reduced; at 4, 8 dB over comes out 2 dB over. Default `10.0`. |
| `release_ms` | number | 1 to 1000 ms to recover when it gets quieter. Default `60.0`. |
| `sidechain_source` | string (optional) | The id of another audio source whose sound drives the reduction instead of this one's (ducking). |
| `threshold_db` | number | −60 to 0 dBFS: where reduction starts. Default `-18.0`. |

## Limiter

Keeps peaks from ever going over a level (OBS's Limiter). Best last in the chain.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `release_ms` | number | 1 to 1000 ms to recover after a peak. Default `60.0`. |
| `threshold_db` | number | −60 to 0 dBFS: no sample comes out louder than this. Default `-6.0`. |

## Expander

Turns down the sound below a threshold, more the quieter it is: a gentler noise gate (OBS's Expander).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `attack_ms` | number | 1 to 100 ms to open up when the sound gets louder. Default `10.0`. |
| `detection` | [Detection](#detection) |  Default `"rms"`. |
| `output_gain_db` | number | −32 to 32 dB added afterwards. Default `0.0`. |
| `ratio` | number | 1 to 20: at 2, sound 10 dB under the threshold comes out 20 dB under; high ratios act like a gate. Default `2.0`. |
| `release_ms` | number | 1 to 1000 ms to turn down when it gets quieter. Default `50.0`. |
| `threshold_db` | number | −60 to 0 dBFS: sound above this is left alone. Default `-40.0`. |

## Detection

How a level-driven filter measures the sound.

One of:

- `"rms"`: The average power over the last 10 ms: steadier, a tone reads 3 dB under its peak.
- `"peak"`: The highest sample: quicker to react.

## UpwardCompressor

Turns up the sound below a threshold, bringing quiet parts closer to loud ones (OBS's Upward Compressor). Sound under −60 dBFS is raised no more than sound at −60 dBFS, so silence and hiss aren't raised without limit.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `attack_ms` | number | 1 to 100 ms to back off when the sound gets louder. Default `10.0`. |
| `detection` | [Detection](#detection) |  Default `"rms"`. |
| `output_gain_db` | number | −32 to 32 dB added afterwards. Default `0.0`. |
| `ratio` | number | 1 to 20: at 2, sound 20 dB under the threshold comes out 10 dB under. Default `2.0`. |
| `release_ms` | number | 1 to 1000 ms to raise it when it gets quieter. Default `50.0`. |
| `threshold_db` | number | −60 to 0 dBFS: sound above this is left alone. Default `-20.0`. |

## Equalizer

Turns the lows, mids and highs up or down (OBS's 3-Band Equalizer). The bands meet at 250 Hz and 4 kHz; at 0 dB each, the sound is unchanged.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `high_db` | number | −20 to 20 dB above 4 kHz. Default `0.0`. |
| `low_db` | number | −20 to 20 dB below 250 Hz. Default `0.0`. |
| `mid_db` | number | −20 to 20 dB from 250 Hz to 4 kHz. Default `0.0`. |

## SourceEncoder

A video source's own ISO file encoding, over `recording.iso.encoder`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bit_depth` | integer (optional) | 8 or 10: this source's ISO file depth, over `recording.iso.encoder.bit_depth` (an 8 here stays 8 even at the incredible preset). 10-bit HEVC uses the Main 10 profile, which avoids banding in gradients, at more encoder work and bigger files; a display, window or application is then also captured in 10 bits. Needs a 10-bit ISO codec (HEVC; ProRes is always 10-bit). Left out, the file follows the recording settings. Max 255. |

## Filter

One filter in a source's chain.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | A filter that is off is skipped. |
| `id` | string (optional) | Identifies the filter for patches; its kind if absent. Unique within its source. |

Plus one of these, chosen by its tag:

- `kind = "color_correction"`: [ColorCorrection](#colorcorrection)
- `kind = "chroma_key"`: [ChromaKey](#chromakey)
- `kind = "color_key"`: [ColorKey](#colorkey)
- `kind = "luma_key"`: [LumaKey](#lumakey)
- `kind = "crop_pad"`: [CropPad](#croppad)
- `kind = "scaling"`: [Scaling](#scaling)
- `kind = "scroll"`: [Scroll](#scroll)
- `kind = "sharpen"`: [Sharpen](#sharpen)
- `kind = "image_mask"`: [ImageMask](#imagemask)
- `kind = "lut"`: [ApplyLut](#applylut)
- `kind = "render_delay"`: [RenderDelay](#renderdelay)
- `kind = "shape_mask"`: [ShapeMask](#shapemask)
- `kind = "gradient_mask"`: [GradientMask](#gradientmask)
- `kind = "source_mask"`: [SourceMask](#sourcemask)

## ColorCorrection

Colour, brightness and opacity changes (OBS's Color Correction).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `brightness` | number | −1 to 1, added to every colour. Default `0.0`. |
| `color_add` | [Color](#color) | Added to every colour, lifting the dark ones; black leaves them. Default `"#000000"`. |
| `color_multiply` | [Color](#color) | Every colour is multiplied by this, tinting the light ones; white leaves them as they are. Default `"#ffffff"`. |
| `contrast` | number | −4 to 4: above 0 spreads colours away from middle grey, below 0 pulls them towards it. Default `0.0`. |
| `gamma` | number | −3 to 3: above 0 lifts the midtones, below 0 darkens them. Default `0.0`. |
| `hue_shift` | number | −180 to 180 degrees around the colour wheel. Default `0.0`. |
| `opacity` | number | 0 (invisible) to 1. Default `1.0`. |
| `saturation` | number | −1 (grey) to 5. Default `0.0`. |

## ChromaKey

Removes a colour by its hue and saturation, whatever its brightness, for green and blue screens (OBS's Chroma Key).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `brightness` | number | −1 to 1, added to every colour. Default `0.0`. |
| `contrast` | number | −4 to 4, as in Color Correction. Default `0.0`. |
| `gamma` | number | −1 to 1: above 0 lifts the midtones. Default `0.0`. |
| `key_color` | [Color](#color) | The colour removed when `key_color_type` is `custom`. Default `"#00ff00"`. |
| `key_color_type` | [KeyColorType](#keycolortype) |  Default `"green"`. |
| `opacity` | number | 0 to 1. Default `1.0`. |
| `similarity` | integer | 1 to 1000: how far from the key colour a pixel may be and still be removed. Higher removes more. Default `400`. |
| `smoothness` | integer | 1 to 1000: how gradually removed areas fade at their edges. Default `80`. |
| `spill` | integer | 1 to 1000: how much of the key colour is taken out of what remains near it, like green fringes on hair. Default `100`. |

## KeyColorType

Which colour a key removes.

One of:

- `"green"` \| `"blue"` \| `"magenta"`
- `"custom"`: The filter's `key_color`.

## ColorKey

Removes one exact colour and those close to it, for graphics and windows (OBS's Color Key).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `brightness` | number | −1 to 1, added to every colour. Default `0.0`. |
| `contrast` | number | −4 to 4, as in Color Correction. Default `0.0`. |
| `gamma` | number | −1 to 1: above 0 lifts the midtones. Default `0.0`. |
| `key_color` | [Color](#color) | The colour removed when `key_color_type` is `custom`. Default `"#00ff00"`. |
| `key_color_type` | [KeyColorType](#keycolortype) |  Default `"green"`. |
| `opacity` | number | 0 to 1. Default `1.0`. |
| `similarity` | integer | 1 to 1000: how far from the key colour a pixel may be and still be removed. Default `80`. |
| `smoothness` | integer | 1 to 1000: how gradually removed areas fade at their edges. Default `50`. |

## LumaKey

Removes the brightest and/or darkest parts (OBS's Luma Key).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `luma_max` | number | 0 to 1: brighter than this is removed. Default `1.0`. |
| `luma_max_smooth` | number | 0 to 1: how far below `luma_max` the removal fades in. Default `0.0`. |
| `luma_min` | number | 0 to 1: darker than this is removed. Default `0.0`. |
| `luma_min_smooth` | number | 0 to 1: how far above `luma_min` the removal fades out. Default `0.0`. |

## CropPad

Cuts pixels from the edges, or adds transparent ones (OBS's Crop/Pad). Unlike an item's crop, it changes the source everywhere it is shown.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `area` | [CropArea](#croparea) (optional) | Instead of edges, the area to keep: its top-left corner and size (OBS's absolute mode). A size of 0 reaches the far edge. |
| `bottom` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `left` | integer | Pixels cut from the left edge; negative adds transparent ones. Default `0`. |
| `right` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `top` | integer |  Default `0`. |

## CropArea

An area of a picture, in its pixels.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `width` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `x` | integer |  Default `0`. |
| `y` | integer |  Default `0`. |

## Scaling

Resizes the picture or changes its shape (OBS's Scaling/Aspect Ratio).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `aspect` | string (optional) | Or a new shape, like "4:3", keeping the height. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `scale_filter` | [ScaleFilter](#scalefilter) |  Default `"bicubic"`. |
| `undistort` | boolean | When narrowing a wide picture, squeeze the sides more and the middle less, so the middle keeps its proportions. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | The new size in pixels (with `height`). |

## Scroll

Moves the picture continuously, wrapping around (OBS's Scroll).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | integer (optional) | Likewise down. |
| `horizontal_speed` | number | Pixels per second; positive moves right. Default `0.0`. |
| `loop` | boolean | Repeat the picture as it scrolls; without it, it scrolls away once. Default `true`. |
| `vertical_speed` | number | Pixels per second; positive moves up. Default `0.0`. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Show only this many pixels across (a window onto the scrolling picture); its own width if absent. |

## Sharpen

Sharpens edges (OBS's Sharpen).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sharpness` | number | 0 to 1. Default `0.07999999821186066`. |

## ImageMask

Masks the picture with an image, or blends an image into it (OBS's Image Mask/Blend).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | [Color](#color) | Which channels a colour mask reads, or the tint of a blend. Default `"#ffffff"`. |
| `mode` | [MaskMode](#maskmode) |  Default `"alpha_mask_color"`. |
| `opacity` | number | 0 to 1: how strongly the image masks or blends. Default `1.0`. |
| `path` (required) | string | The image: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. |
| `stretch` | boolean | Stretch the image over the picture; otherwise it keeps its shape and covers the picture, centred, its overflow cut off. |

## MaskMode

How an image masks or blends with the picture.

One of:

- `"alpha_mask_color"`: The image's colour (the channels `color` names; white: all of them) sets how much of the picture shows.
- `"alpha_mask_alpha"`: The image's transparency sets how much of the picture shows.
- `"blend_multiply"`: The picture's colours multiplied by the image's.
- `"blend_add"`: The image's colours added to the picture's.
- `"blend_subtract"`: The image's colours taken from the picture's.

## ApplyLut

Colour grading with a lookup table (OBS's Apply LUT).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number | 0 (off) to 1 (full). Default `1.0`. |
| `path` (required) | string | A .cube file, or a .png LUT (512×512 tiles or a strip): absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. |

## RenderDelay

Shows the picture later, to line it up with sound that arrives late (OBS's Render Delay). Recordings only: a snapshot shows the moment.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `delay_ms` | integer | 0 to 500 milliseconds. Default `0`. |

## ShapeMask

Shows the picture inside a shape (OBS Advanced Masks' shape masks).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `animations` | list of [MaskAnimation](#maskanimation) | Animations of its numbers (see [`MaskAnimation`]). |
| `combine` | [MaskCombine](#maskcombine) |  Default `"intersect"`. |
| `feather` | number | Softens the edge over this many pixels, centred on it. Default `0.0`. |
| `height` | number | Its height as a fraction of the picture's. Default `0.800000011920929`. |
| `inner_radius` | number | How far a star's notches reach out, as a fraction of its points' reach: 0.05 to 1. Default `0.5`. |
| `invert` | boolean | Show the picture outside the shape instead. |
| `points` | integer | A star's points: 3 to 32. Default `5`. |
| `radius` | [Radius](#radius) | Rounds corners, in pixels: each of a rectangle's (top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left), or a polygon's and star's (the first value). |
| `rotation` | number | Turns the shape about its centre, in degrees clockwise. Default `0.0`. |
| `shape` | [MaskShape](#maskshape) |  Default `"rectangle"`. |
| `sides` | integer | A polygon's sides: 3 to 32. Default `6`. |
| `width` | number | The shape's box: its width as a fraction of the picture's. Default `0.800000011920929`. |
| `x` | number | Where the shape's centre is across the picture: 0 (left edge) to 1 (right edge). Default `0.5`. |
| `y` | number | And down: 0 (top) to 1 (bottom). Default `0.5`. |

## MaskAnimation

Animates a mask's numbers over time, as an item's `animations` do (CSS's `animation`), with its stops written in place: each stop sets some of the mask's numbers by their field names.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `delay_ms` | integer | How long after its clock starts it starts, in milliseconds; less than 0 starts it part of the way through. |
| `direction` | [PlayDirection](#playdirection) | |
| `duration_ms` (required) | integer | How long one run takes, in milliseconds. |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) | How each stretch between stops speeds up and slows down, unless a stop says otherwise: `ease_in_out` if absent. |
| `fill` | [Fill](#fill) | |
| `frames` (required) | list of [MaskKeyframe](#maskkeyframe) | The stops, in order of `at`. A number no stop at 0 (or 1) sets runs from (or to) the mask's own value. |
| `iterations` | [Iterations](#iterations) | How many runs: a number (1 if absent) or `"infinite"`. |
| `start` | [AnimationStart](#animationstart) | The clock it runs on: `clock` (the engine's: loops stay in step, in the program and in filtered ISO files and previews alike), or `on_air` and `shown` (both: from when the masked source's picture is first drawn). Snapshots show animations at their start. |

## MaskKeyframe

One stop of a mask animation: the mask's numbers at `at`. Each kind of mask animates its own: shape masks `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `rotation`, `radius`, `inner_radius` and `feather`; gradient masks `x`, `y`, `angle`, `length` and `feather`; source masks `x`, `y`, `scale`, `threshold` and `softness`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number (optional) | |
| `at` (required) | number | How far through a run it is, from 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). |
| `easing` | [Easing](#easing) (optional) | How the stretch from this stop to the next speeds up and slows down, in place of the animation's `easing`. |
| `feather` | number (optional) | |
| `height` | number (optional) | |
| `inner_radius` | number (optional) | |
| `length` | number (optional) | |
| `radius` | [Radius](#radius) (optional) | |
| `rotation` | number (optional) | |
| `scale` | number (optional) | |
| `softness` | number (optional) | |
| `threshold` | number (optional) | |
| `width` | number (optional) | |
| `x` | number (optional) | |
| `y` | number (optional) | |

## MaskCombine

How a mask combines with the masks before it in the chain.

One of:

- `"intersect"`: Only what this mask and those before it both show stays (the first mask simply masks).
- `"add"`: What this mask shows is added to what those before it show (of the picture before them).
- `"subtract"`: What this mask shows is taken away from what those before it show.

## MaskShape

A shape mask's shape.

One of:

- `"rectangle"`: Fills its box, with each corner rounded by `radius`.
- `"circle"`: The largest circle that fits its box.
- `"ellipse"`: Fills its box.
- `"polygon"`: A regular polygon with `sides`, the largest that fits its box, a corner at the top; corners rounded by `radius`.
- `"star"`: A star with `points`, the largest that fits its box, a point at the top; `inner_radius` sets how deep its notches go.
- `"heart"`: A heart, the largest that fits its box.

## GradientMask

Fades the picture in or out along a gradient (OBS Advanced Masks' gradient masks).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `angle` | number | A linear gradient's direction, in degrees clockwise: 0 runs left to right, 90 top to bottom. Default `0.0`. |
| `animations` | list of [MaskAnimation](#maskanimation) | Animations of its numbers (see [`MaskAnimation`]). |
| `combine` | [MaskCombine](#maskcombine) |  Default `"intersect"`. |
| `feather` | number | Softens the gradient over this many more pixels. Default `0.0`. |
| `gradient` | [GradientShape](#gradientshape) |  Default `"linear"`. |
| `invert` | boolean | Show where the gradient hides, and hide where it shows. |
| `length` | number | How long it is: 1 spans the picture along its direction (linear), or reaches its corners from the middle (radial). Default `1.0`. |
| `stops` | list of [GradientStop](#gradientstop) | How much shows along it, from its start to its end (2 to 8 stops, in order of `at`); between stops it changes evenly. Before the first and after the last, their opacity holds. Default `[{"at": 0.0, "opacity": 1.0}, {"at": 1.0, "opacity": 0.0}]`. |
| `x` | number | The gradient's centre across the picture: 0 (left) to 1 (right). Default `0.5`. |
| `y` | number | And down: 0 (top) to 1 (bottom). Default `0.5`. |

## GradientShape

A gradient mask's shape.

One of:

- `"linear"`: Changes along a line through its centre, in the direction `angle`.
- `"radial"`: Changes outwards from its centre.

## GradientStop

One stop of a gradient mask.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `at` (required) | number | Where along the gradient: 0 (its start) to 1 (its end). |
| `opacity` (required) | number | How much of the picture shows there: 0 (none) to 1 (all). |

## SourceMask

Uses another source's or scene's live picture as the mask (OBS Advanced Masks' source masks), frame by frame in step with the program. Until the mask has a picture, nothing of the source shows, whatever `invert`, `threshold` or `combine` say. Previews of the source alone, and its ISO file, show it unmasked by other sources.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `animations` | list of [MaskAnimation](#maskanimation) | Animations of its numbers (see [`MaskAnimation`]). |
| `channel` | [MaskChannel](#maskchannel) |  Default `"luminance"`. |
| `combine` | [MaskCombine](#maskcombine) |  Default `"intersect"`. |
| `fit` | [MaskFit](#maskfit) |  Default `"stretch"`. |
| `invert` | boolean | Show the picture where the mask would hide it, and hide it where it would show. |
| `mask_scene` | string (optional) | Or the id of a scene, drawn on its own canvas, that masks. |
| `mask_source` | string (optional) | The id of the video source whose picture masks (give it or `mask_scene`). It runs, and is on air (media play, pages load), while a source it masks does. |
| `scale` | number | Scales the mask's picture about its centre, after `fit`. Default `1.0`. |
| `softness` | number | How gradually it turns, 0 (at once: a hard edge) to 1 (evenly from 0 to 1, which with a threshold of 0.5 uses the value as it is). Default `1.0`. |
| `threshold` | number | With `softness`, where the channel's value turns from hiding to showing the picture: 0 to 1. Default `0.5`. |
| `x` | number | Where the mask's centre is across the masked picture: 0 (left) to 1 (right). Default `0.5`. |
| `y` | number | And down: 0 (top) to 1 (bottom). Default `0.5`. |

## MaskChannel

What a source mask reads of the mask's picture.

One of:

- `"red"` \| `"green"` \| `"blue"`
- `"luminance"`: Its brightness: white shows the picture, black (or transparent) hides it. Right for black-and-white mask videos.
- `"alpha"`: Its opacity: opaque shows the picture, transparent hides it.

## MaskFit

How a source mask's picture is placed on the masked picture before `scale`, `x` and `y` move it.

One of:

- `"stretch"`: Stretched over the whole picture.
- `"contain"`: As large as fits inside, keeping its shape; outside it nothing shows.
- `"cover"`: Covers the picture, keeping its shape; its overflow is cut off.
- `"none"`: Pixel for pixel, at its own size.

## DisplaySource

A whole display (OBS's macOS Screen Capture, display mode).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | boolean | Show the mouse pointer. Default `true`. |
| `display` | string | "main", or a display's name or id from `isocast devices`. Default `"main"`. |

## WindowSource

One window (OBS's macOS Screen Capture, window mode), matched by its app and optionally its title; the largest match wins. It keeps its size if the window is resized, scaling the window to fit. On Linux the first start asks for the window in the desktop's sharing dialog instead, and the source reopens that window by its id.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `app` (required) | string | The app's name or bundle id, or part of the name. |
| `cursor` | boolean | Show the mouse pointer. Default `true`. |
| `title` | string (optional) | Part of the window's title. |

## ApplicationSource

Every window of an app on a display (OBS's macOS Screen Capture, application mode), at the display's size.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `app` (required) | string | The app's name or bundle id, or part of the name. |
| `cursor` | boolean | Show the mouse pointer. Default `true`. |
| `display` | string | "main", or a display's name or id. Default `"main"`. |

## ApplicationAudioSource

The sound of one app (OBS's Application Audio Capture).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `app` (required) | string | A stable app id from `devices`, or the app's name or bundle id, or part of the name on macOS. macOS matches substrings; Linux names and executable aliases match exactly, case-insensitively (stable ids are case-sensitive). |

## CameraSource

A camera, capture card, Continuity Camera, or an iPhone or iPad screen over USB. Without `width`/`height`/`fps`, the camera's best format is used: the highest frame rate up to the canvas fps, then the largest size that fits on the canvas either way round (else the smallest larger one).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `device` (required) | string | An id from `isocast devices`, a name, or part of a name (the shortest name containing it wins). |
| `fps` | integer (optional) | |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `width` | integer (optional) | |

## MicrophoneSource

A microphone or audio interface input.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `channels` | list of integer (optional) | Which of the device's input channels to record, numbered from 1 as `isocast devices` lists them: one (`[1]`, a mic on input 1) is recorded as centred mono at full level; two (`[1, 2]`, `[3, 4]`) as left and right. Absent records inputs 1 and 2 as left and right (a 1-input device's input as one channel), on larger interfaces too; pick other inputs here. |
| `device` | string | "default", or an id, name or part of a name from `isocast devices`. Default `"default"`. |

## SystemAudioSource

Audio the computer is playing, optionally leaving some apps out.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `exclude` | list of string | Apps whose sound is left out: names or bundle ids, or parts of names, as for `application_audio`'s `app` (`isocast devices` lists the apps that have opened audio). |

## ColorSource

A solid colour (OBS's Color Source).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` (required) | [Color](#color) | `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Size in pixels; the canvas size if absent. |

## SlideshowSource

Images shown one after another (OBS's Image Slide Show), each fitted inside the slide show's size and centred.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `files` (required) | list of string | Image files, in order: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `loop` | boolean | Start again after the last image (else stay on it). Default `true`. |
| `shuffle` | boolean | Show the images in a random order. Default `false`. |
| `slide_ms` | integer | How long each image shows, in milliseconds. Default `8000`. |
| `transition` | [Transition](#transition) | How one image changes to the next (a fade by default). Default `{"duration_ms": 700, "kind": "fade"}`. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Size in pixels; the first image's size if absent. |

## MediaSource

Video and audio files (OBS's Media Source): one file, or a playlist played in order. Its sound goes into the mixer like any audio source.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `files` (required) | list of string | Files to play, in order: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. MOV, MP4, M4A, MP3, WAV and anything else macOS can decode. |
| `loop` | boolean | Start again after the last file (else hold its last frame). Default `false`. |
| `restart_on_activate` | boolean | Play from the start each time the program shows it, and not while it is off air (else it plays all along). Media without video is on air while a scene on air has an item for it; with no item in any scene it always plays. Default `true`. |
| `speed` | number | Playback speed, 0.25 to 4; sound changes pitch with it. Default `1.0`. |

## BrowserSource

A web page (OBS's Browser Source), rendered by WebKit at a set size, transparent where the page is.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `control_audio` | boolean | Send the page's sound to the mixer as this source's audio, instead of playing it aloud (OBS's "Control audio via OBS"). |
| `css` | string | CSS added to the page (OBS's default makes the page transparent). Default `"body { background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); margin: 0px auto; overflow: hidden; }"`. |
| `file` | string (optional) | Or a local HTML file: absolute, `~/...`, or relative to the setup file. |
| `fps` | integer | Frames drawn per second. Default `30`. |
| `height` | integer |  Default `600`. |
| `refresh_when_shown` | boolean | Reload the page each time the program shows it again (OBS's "Refresh browser when scene becomes active"). |
| `shutdown_when_hidden` | boolean | Unload the page while the program doesn't show it, and load it afresh when it does (OBS's "Shutdown source when not visible"). |
| `url` | string (optional) | An http(s) or file URL. |
| `width` | integer | The page's size in CSS pixels. Default `800`. |

## TestPatternSource

Synthetic video that needs no permissions: moving colour bars, a frame counter and a burnt-in clock. It flashes for 100 ms at every whole second of the session clock, in step with `tone` beeps.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fps` | integer |  Default `60`. |
| `height` | integer |  Default `1080`. |
| `width` | integer |  Default `1920`. |

## ToneSource

Synthetic stereo audio that needs no permissions: a 100 ms beep at every whole second of the session clock.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `frequency` | integer | Beep pitch in Hz. Default `1000`. |

## VirtualCameraSettings

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `canvas` | string (optional) | The extra canvas (a `[[canvases]]` id, or `vertical`), for target = canvas (#120). |
| `height` | integer (optional) | |
| `scene` | string (optional) | |
| `source` | string (optional) | |
| `target` | [Target](#target) | Program, studio preview, the vertical program, or an explicit scene/source id. Default `"program"`. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Output dimensions; both absent uses the canvas (the vertical canvas's for target = vertical, the extra canvas's for target = canvas). Other aspect ratios are letterboxed. These are the camera extension's advertised modes. |

## Target

One of:

- `"program"` \| `"preview"` \| `"scene"` \| `"source"`
- `"vertical"`: The vertical canvas's program (`[vertical]` must be on).
- `"canvas"`: An extra canvas's program (`canvas`: a `[[canvases]]` id, #120).
